title: Weights & Caches: LLMs Can Program Tabular Foundation Models

target_networks.name: TabPFN-3.5 (pretrained tabular foundation model; weights and KV cache)

tasks_benchmarks: synthetic flip-the-slope and sine-to-square-wave (10 unseen datasets each)

headline_result.text: Astra wrote nanoTabPFN from zero weights without running it, reaching mean ROC AUC 0.849 on 20 TabArena datasets versus 0.876 for a pretrained baseline, and repaired a TabPFN-3.5 signed-product failure (median R2 about 0 to 0.991-0.998) with 0.08% average error increase on TabArena-Lite.
headline_result.quote: First, Astra directly programs nanoTabPFN from zero-initialized weights, achiev- ing a mean ROC AUC of 0.849 across 20 TabArena datasets, compared to 0.876 for a pretrained baseline.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: nanoTabPFN: 2 sessions, better one reported; repair: 1 session; KV-cache steering: 1 session per task

key_claims.claim: The written nanoTabPFN implements a multiscale kernel naive Bayes classifier and filled in only 0.42% of the weights.
key_claims.quote: Notably, only 0.42% of the weights were filled in, which can be indicative of overparametrization of nanoTabPFN.

key_claims.claim: The written network had higher AUC than the trained baseline on only 3 of 20 datasets.
key_claims.quote: WSP-NanoTabPFN has the higher AUC on 3 of the 20 datasets

key_claims.claim: The signed-product repair passed all fixed success criteria while leaving TabArena-Lite error nearly unchanged.
key_claims.quote: On TabArena-Lite, the geometric-mean edited-to-pretrained error ratio is 1.0008 (95% confidence interval: 0.9999–1.0017), indicating little aggregate change on the preservation bench- mark.

key_claims.claim: The repair changed about 105 million weight entries, so it does not show that a small local edit suffices, and transfer beyond targeted regimes is partial.
key_claims.quote: Transfer beyond the targeted regimes is partial. The intervention also changes approximately 105 million weight entries, so it does not establish that a small local edit suffices.

key_claims.claim: Astra-written KV-cache editing programs approximately flipped slopes and turned sines into square waves on unseen datasets without changing weights, with varying quality.
key_claims.quote: Both programs ap- proximate the intended transformations on previously unseen datasets, although the quality of the interventions varies across datasets.

limitations_stated.text: Controls support the constructed sign computation but do not show that the pretrained model already contained the full circuit.
limitations_stated.quote: they do not establish that the pretrained model already contained the complete circuit.

limitations_stated.text: The findings are described as exploratory.

notes_for_review: Extends WSP to tabular foundation models in three settings: writing nanoTabPFN from zero weights with no forward passes (strict, audited), repairing a real TabPFN-3.5 failure with a tool-using agent and closed-form fits, and programming KV-cache edits. The construction result is credible and the written algorithm is interpretable; the repair is not a small edit (125 tensors, ~105M entries) and used closed-form ridge solves, so it is closer to analytic engineering than hand-written weights. Single sessions (the best of two for construction), no random-edit or fine-tuning comparison for the repair, and no code release is stated.
